newsitem.title: USA: Brent slips in late U.S. trading, activity thin.
newsitem.headline: Brent slips in late U.S. trading, activity thin.

text.p: North Sea Brent slipped in late U.S. trading Monday although activity was especially thin in light of gas oil-related jitters in Europe, traders said.
Partial paper March Brents changed hands twice at $22.03 a barrel and once at $22.04, down from $22.05 at the IPE settlement, traders said.
February/March Brent traded at 39 cents, with the spread talked at 37-40 cents. March/April was done at 38.5 cents, and was also talked at 37-40 cents a barrel, traders said.
Meanwhile, North Sea sellers continue to target the U.S. Gulf Coast, reflecting the open transatlantic arbitrage, traders said.
The spread between West Texas Intermediate/Cushing and Brent for March was around $1.65-75 cents a barrel.
At least three companies are offering Brent cargoes into the Gulf for the first half of March around March WTI minus 30 cents a barrel delivered, traders said.
